rounds.reasoning:
Bash was blocked in this session, so pixel-level numbers below are estimated from the rendered image (720×1080, 80×60 cells → ~9px/col, 18px/row) plus `cells.txt` directly.

## 1. What is literally there

A vertical poster. A thin gray border frames a picture area; inside it, a mid-blue field divided by gray bars into a rough window-pane grid. Over that, a large teal/cyan **hand** — palm toward the viewer, four fingers up, thumb splayed left — with a vertical forearm running from the palm straight down to the bottom edge. Flanking the lower half, solid black blobs read as foliage or branches in silhouette. A black header band carries letter-spaced `A G A I N S T   T H E   P A N E`; a footer rule carries `opus / AGENTSCII` and the title again.

Palette is essentially five flats: gray frame, one blue, one teal, one lighter cyan, black — plus scattered periwinkle/violet stray pixels. The subject *is* recognizable at a glance. That much is real.

## 2. Concrete defects

**a) Literal ASCII density ramp used as fill — rows 38–54, cols 38–48.**
Seventeen consecutive rows contain the byte-identical string `░ █ ▓ ▒ ░ ░` at the same columns. That is the textbook `█▓▒░` shading ramp pasted unchanged, and it lands exactly on the forearm (render y≈684–972, x≈340–435). Not shading — a placeholder strip.

**b) The forearm is a constant-width rectangle.** y≈650→972, no taper, no wrist, no overlap with the palm, terminating in a flush horizontal cut at the picture edge. Consistent with (a).

**c) The hand is unshaded.** Every finger is a single teal value. The only tonal variation is one hard-edged lighter-cyan blob on the palm (x≈230–380, y≈480–545) with a step edge on all four sides. It reads as a fill spill, not a light source. No form modeling anywhere on a subject occupying ~40% of the canvas.

**d) Window grid is incoherent.** A vertical mullion at col ≈21 (x≈195) splits both the upper and lower bands, but there is no matching mullion on the right — so the right "pane" is ~3× the width of the left in both bands. Not a window; two arbitrary partitions.

**e) Frame edges are serrated combs, not lines.** `cells.txt` rows 6–18 alternate ` ▒ ░` / ` ▒ ░░` at cols 1–4, and col 80 alternates `░`/blank. Rendered, the left frame edge and the header band's left/right edges (x≈35–45, x≈665–675) are saw-toothed. Same comb reappears along the bottom band.

**f) Horizontal scanline seams.**
- Row 19 is a full-width alternating dither `░ ░ ░ ░ ░ ░ ░ ░ ░ ░` → visible seam at y≈340.
- Row 37 has a 10-char `▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀` run at cols 10–19 → streak across the lower-left pane, y≈665.
- Row 50 has a 15-char `▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀` run at cols 49–64 → hard horizontal bar at right, y≈900.
These cut straight through the foliage silhouettes and read as banding glitches, not marks.

**g) Foliage is undifferentiated black void.** The blobs at x≈45–190 / y≈680–880 and x≈510–600 / y≈660–970 have zero internal structure — no branch, leaf, or edge articulation. The right-hand blob at x≈620–660, y≈365–430 floats unconnected to anything. Silhouette broken by the seams in (f).

**h) Uncorrected violet noise.** Periwinkle pixels scattered along finger edges (x≈250/y≈145, x≈530/y≈250) and as patches in the lower-left (x≈80–180, y≈560–650) and lower-right (x≈570–620, y≈540–620) panes. No compositional role; reads as a quantization artifact.

**i) Glyph layer is decorrelated from the image.** Comparing `cells.txt` to the render: the picture is carried almost entirely by cell *background* color. The character layer is diagonal `▓ ▓ ▓` lattices (rows 25–34), scattered `▀` speckle, and the ramp in (a) — generic texture that does not follow the hand's form, the frame, or the foliage. Strip the glyphs and you lose nothing.

**j) Generator slug baked in.** `opus / AGENTSCII` in the footer, with the title repeated a third time below it.

## 3. Verdict

It clears the bar of "geometric placeholder" — there is a real, legible subject. But the execution underneath is not finished work: a copy-pasted density ramp doing the job of the forearm across 17 identical rows, a completely unshaded main subject with one hard-edged blob for "light," an asymmetric non-window frame with combed edges, and three glitch scanlines cutting the silhouette. The recognizability is doing all the work; the craft isn't there.

VERDICT: REJECT

A four-color image — pure black, a saturated blue (`#2222ee`-ish), a bright cyan, and a mid gray — no midtones between them.

- **Subject:** a large cyan open hand, palm toward the viewer, fingers pointing up. Occupies roughly rows 3–32, cols 24–58. Four upward digits plus a separate cyan blob at left (rows ~19–26, cols ~11–23) that reads as a thumb.

- **Background:** blue dithered field with gray structural bars — two verticals near cols 3 and 75, horizontals at rows 14–15 and 46–47. Reads as a window mullion or grid frame.
- **Footer plate:** `opus / AGENTSCII` (white), `CONTACT` (cyan), `2026-09-24` (white), between two rule lines.

## 2. Concrete defects

- **Hard-coded border strips.** Cols 1–5 are the literal string `▒▒▀░░` on every one of rows 1–50, with no variation. Cols 76–80 are `▒▒▀░░`/`▒▒░░░` alternating per row, equally invariant. That's a stamped constant, not drawn content — ~12% of the canvas is filler.

- **Flat unshaded palm.** Rows ~25–32, cols ~33–47 are one uniform cyan with zero gradient or falloff. The cell data there is a solid `████████`/`▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓` slab (rows 24–31) — a fill, not shading.
- **Banding.** The column at rows 33–50, cols 33–42 is alternating horizontal stripes of teal/darker teal. It reads as a sampling artifact, not as cylindrical form. Similar streaking across the lower palm, rows 28–33.
- **Flat black masses.** Rows 34–50, cols 5–22 and 48–63 are pure black with no internal detail whatsoever — only a jagged outer edge. Roughly a quarter of the image is unrendered.
- **Broken silhouette.** The thumb blob (rows ~19–26, cols ~11–23) is disconnected from the palm by a black gap; it floats as a separate object. The right side of the hand (rows ~17–23, cols ~48–58) dissolves into background noise — the outer finger has no closed contour.

The background thirds are near-uniform `▒`/`░`/`▀` noise regardless of what's on screen. Density tracks luminance in the hand, and nowhere else.
- **Baked-in generator stamp.** `opus /` in the footer is a model tag, not a caption. `CONTACT` and a bare date are placeholder-grade titling.
- **Trailing blank rows** at 51 and 57.

The subject is recognizable — this is not a geometric placeholder, and the finger and palm structure genuinely exists in the cell data. But the execution is unfinished: the palm is a flat fill, the lower third is flat black next to a banded stripe, the borders are a repeated constant, the thumb is severed from the hand, and the ASCII layer stops describing the image outside the central figure. Two of the four colors do no shading work at all.

VERDICT: REJECT

A 80×56 character grid, 720×1024 px, rendered in a five-color palette: bright cyan, teal, medium blue, dark navy/black, and light gray.

The dominant subject is legible: a **hand**, palm facing the viewer, five fingers spread and pointing up, thumb on the left. It fills roughly the upper two-thirds. It's rendered in two cyan tones against blue. The fingers have real gaps between them, taper slightly, and the thumb is correctly offset and lower — this is an actual constructed silhouette, not a blob.

Overlaid on everything is a **gray grid/frame**: vertical bars at cols 1–5, 21–23, and 74–80, plus a horizontal bar at rows 14–15. Reads as a window mullion or pane divider in front of the hand.

Below the wrist (~row 32) the image loses subject entirely: a dark navy/black horizontal mass with a vertical light-blue ladder-striped column running down the center (render x≈300–340), flanked by heavily banded blue. No recognizable form.

Bottom plate: two full-width rules with three lines of text — `opus / AGENTSCII`, `CONTACT`, `2026-09-24`.

## 2. Concrete defects

**Verbatim copy-pasted slab.** Rows 32–35, cols 8–13 are the identical string `▓█████` four rows running. A solid 6×4 rectangle with zero internal variation. Row 30–31 are near-identical offsets of the same slab. This is fill, not drawing.

These are evenly-spaced rectangles, and they do not follow the hand silhouette at all.

**The character layer is decoupled from the subject.** This is the central problem. The hand's silhouette is carried almost entirely by per-cell foreground/background *color*. The glyph layer underneath is generic ▒/░ dither noise plus the block slabs above. Strip the color and there is no hand. For a piece presented as character art, the characters are doing decoration, not construction.

**Mechanically tiled frame texture.** Cols 1–5 are the literal string `▒▒▀░░` repeated on all 50 rows; cols 76–80 alternate `▒▒░░░`/`▒▒▀░░` on a fixed 2-row period; cols 21–23 alternate `▀░▒`/`░░▒` on a 2-row period. The dashed white/gray checker on the mullions is a constant-period stamp down the full height with no variation, no interaction with what it crosses, and no shading.

**Large flat unshaded regions.**
- Rows 1–13, cols 55–75 (top right): near-solid ░ — flat medium blue, no modeling.
- Rows 37–50, cols 41–48: an unbroken vertical band of ░ — flat, 14 rows tall.
- The palm interior (approx rows 25–33, cols 30–46) is a single flat cyan. A palm-forward hand has knuckle pads, a thenar mound, and finger-base shadow. None present.

**Horizontal banding.** Rows 36–50 across the full width are long horizontal runs of uniform ▒ broken by single-row ▀ streaks — reads in the render as scanline banding across the entire lower half.

**Frame bar occludes the fingers without any depth cue.** The row 14–15 bar cuts flat through the middle/ring fingers. Same flat gray, same dash pattern, no shadow, no edge, no contact — so it reads as a rendering artifact cutting the hand in half rather than as glass or a mullion in front of it.

**Illegible lower 40%.** Rows 32–50 have no readable subject. The ladder-striped column below the wrist is neither an arm, a sleeve, nor a body; the dark masses at rows 26–31 cols 58–72 and rows 18–24 cols 60–72 are unresolved black shapes with no form.

**Stray detached pixels.** Cyan fragments float outside the finger silhouette around rows 5–8, cols 30–33, and the fingertip edges at rows 3–5 are ragged single-cell noise rather than a defined tip.

**Baked-in metadata.** `opus / AGENTSCII` is a generator/model label composited into the image. `CONTACT` sits as an untitled one-word caption. This is tooling chrome, not part of the piece.

**Blank row.** Row 51 is entirely spaces, between the art and the rule.

## 3. Verdict

The hand is real work and I'll credit it — the digit spacing, thumb placement, and taper are deliberate. But it's one good passage inside an otherwise unfinished frame: the bottom 40% has no subject, the border is a repeated stamp, there is a literally copy-pasted `█████` rectangle, the palm and the whole top-right quadrant are unshaded flats, and the glyph layer isn't carrying the image — color is. Remove the color and nothing survives. That's the tell for a piece that was composited rather than constructed.

VERDICT: REJECT

Proportions are broadly right: eyes at ~42% of head height, mouth at ~75%, mouth center (col 39) sitting almost exactly between the two eye centers (32 and 48).

The right third (cols ~50–70, rows 3–27) is a field of loose violet/magenta and dark-brick dots in vertical striations. No form in it.

Footer: a `═══` rule, `opus / AGENTSCII`, `WHAT THE FIRE IS TAKING`, another rule.

## 2. Concrete defects

**Both silhouette edges are ruler-straight.** Rows 8–16 all begin at *exactly* col 26 — nine consecutive rows, an unbroken vertical left contour spanning about a third of the head's height. On the right, a `▐` glyph holds cols 45→48 across rows 4–22, rendering as a hard vermilion stripe from the crown to below the mouth. A skull curves on both sides; this one is a slab with a rounded lid.

**Horizontal banding across the forehead/crown**, rows 8–11, cols 30–45. Row 10 runs seven identical `▓` in a row; row 8 runs `░░░░░░░` then `▒▒▒▒▒▒` then `▓▓▓`. Stacked constant-density terraces with hard steps and zero variation along any row. The whole upper head is stratified, not modeled.

**The right field is a per-row gradient function, not a form.** Rows 8–18 each carry the identical left-to-right density profile (`▒▒▒` → `░░░░░░` → `░ ░ ░`). Thirteen rows, same ramp, no vertical variation. Charitably it's the head dissolving into embers, which the title supports — but a dissolve needs form to dissolve *from*, and this is a gradient applied uniformly per row. The hue also breaks the palette: violet against an otherwise red/orange/yellow fire scheme. Embers don't go purple.

**One stamp does all three features.** The left eye, the right eye, and the mouth are the same construction: horizontal `▀`/`▄` rule, dark `██` core, second rule. An eye and a mouth are different objects and should not be built identically. This is a motif placed three times, not three observed forms.

**No nose.** Cols 37–45, rows 16–20 — the exact center of the face — is undifferentiated `▒▒▒▒▓▓▒▒` mid-density fill. No bridge, no tip, no nostril, no cast shadow. The feature that establishes a head's volume is blank.

**Right eye collides with the silhouette.** The eye occupies cols 46–50 while the `▐` edge bar sits at cols 47–48 on neighboring rows. The eye is inside the outline, falling off the edge of the face, with no temple or cheek beyond it.

**Flat unshaded jaw/neck.** Rows 26–27 are `░░░░░░░` and `░░░░░░░░░` — eight and nine identical cells. The head doesn't terminate in a jaw; it fades into a uniform wash. Silhouette unresolved at the bottom.

**Orphan cells.** Isolated `█` blocks float at cols 50–53 across rows 7–22, disconnected from both the head and the dither field. A stray `░` sits alone at col 32 on rows 26, 27, and 28, below and left of the jaw.

**Caption text:** `opus / AGENTSCII` is a build/model stamp rather than a signature, but it is not debug output, a placeholder string, or lorem ipsum. I'm not counting it as a defect of that kind.

## 3. Assessment

A subject does resolve, and the eye and mouth cells were deliberately placed — that's real. But the silhouette is straight-edged on both sides, the forehead is terraced bands, the nose is missing entirely, all three features come from one stamp, and a quarter of the canvas is a per-row ramp in a color that doesn't belong to the piece. That is a geometric assembly with a face's landmarks positioned correctly on it, not a constructed head.

Internally: the top third (rows 4–11) is a fairly uniform brown dithered dome. Below it, rows 12–25 are a dense scramble of yellow vertical streaks and red/crimson clots. Rows 16–19 hold two darker block clusters side by side (cols ~30–37 and ~38–45). Row 25 is a hard horizontal `▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀` rule (cols 33–40). Rows 26–27 are a sparse, gappy fringe below that. Along the right side, cols ~48–58, rows 7–27, there's a trailing haze of isolated `·` and `░` dots in olive/yellow that sits *outside* the oval.

Recognizable subject: a **head** — brown hair/scorched mass on top, a brow band, an eye-level band, a jawline, neck stubs. It resolves as a head, but weakly. It does not resolve as a *face*: I cannot point at an eye and say that's an eye.

## 2. Concrete defects

- **Banding / scanline artifacts.** Row 25 cols 33–40 is eight identical `▀` in a row — a straight ruled line doing the job of a jaw. Same problem at row 10 cols 32–34 (`▀▀▀`), row 11 cols 33–38 (`███▀▀▀`) and cols 44–46, row 18 cols 37–40 (`▀▀▀▀`), row 21 cols 36–39, row 22 cols 27–30 (`▄▄▄`). These read as horizontal stripes laid across the form, not as modeled edges.
- **Flat unshaded region.** Rows 4–9, cols ~26–50: the entire cranium is near-uniform brown `░`/`▒` with almost no value break. It's a filled zone, not a shaded one. Compare the churn immediately below it — the transition at row 10 is abrupt, not a gradient.
- **Posterization.** Yellow abuts crimson abuts black with no intermediate step anywhere in rows 12–25. Four tones, no midtones. Everything hotter than mid reads as one flat yellow.
- **Illegible construction where the features should be.** Rows 16–18, cols 30–45. There are two dark clusters roughly where eyes belong, but the left one (`█▒▒▓▓▒▌`, row 16 cols 30–36) is a solid block and the right one (row 17–18 cols 38–45) dissolves into the cheek. They are different sizes, different shapes, different values, and not on a shared baseline. Nose and mouth (rows 19–23) are indistinguishable from the surrounding noise — row 22's `▄▄▒▓▓█▓▒▒▄` is the only mouth candidate and it does not read as one.
- **Broken / leaking silhouette.** The left edge is a hard boundary; the right edge is not. Cols ~48–58 across rows 7–27 are orphan dots floating outside the outline (row 9 cols ~48–56, row 20 cols ~53–58, row 23 cols ~50–57). The result is an asymmetric form that dissolves on one side only. If that's meant as smoke or ash, it's applied to one side with no counterpart and no density falloff, so it reads as stray dither rather than intent.
- **Unfinished bottom.** Row 26 has literal blank cells *inside* the form — cols 35–38 and col 41 are spaces, punching holes in the neck. Row 27 has the same at col 41. Row 28 is entirely empty: the head terminates with no shoulders, no body, nothing. The piece stops rather than ends.
- **No debug or placeholder strings.** The only text is the intentional title card at rows 31–32. That's chrome, not a defect.

## 3. Assessment

There's real per-cell work here — glyph choice does track form in places (the brow at rows 10–11, the jaw arc at 22–25), so this isn't a geometric primitive with a filter on it. But the payoff isn't there. The subject is a head only by silhouette; every feature that would make it a *portrait* is either a ruled horizontal band or noise. The cranium is flat fill. The right side leaks. The neck has holes in it and nothing below. This is a mid-stage render someone stopped working on, not a finished piece.
